Every interface separating a black cluster from a red cluster is shown in green. This random collection of interfaces converges in law to CLE<sub>6</sub> as the lattice spacing goes to zero.]]

[[File:SLE6 Percolation Interface.pdf|thumb|To define a random interface converging to SLE, we fix the colors of the hexagons along the boundary of the domain. This procedure defines a single interface separating red hexagons from black hexagons. This path converges in law to SLE<sub>6</sub> as the lattice spacing goes to zero.]]

A '''conformal loop ensemble''' ('''CLE'''<sub>κ</sub>) is a random collection of non-crossing loops in a simply connected, open subset of the plane. These random collections of loops are indexed by a parameter κ, which may be any [[real number]] between 8/3 and 8. CLE<sub>κ</sub> is a loop version of the [[Schramm–Loewner evolution]]: SLE<sub>κ</sub> is designed to model a single discrete random interface, while CLE<sub>κ</sub> models a full collection of interfaces.

In many instances for which there is a conjectured or proved relationship between a discrete model and SLE<sub>κ</sub>, there is also a conjectured or proved relationship with CLE<sub>κ</sub>. For example:

*CLE<sub>3</sub> is the limit of interfaces for the critical [[Ising model]].
*CLE<sub>4</sub> may be viewed as the 0-set of the [[Gaussian free field]].
*CLE<sub>16/3</sub> is a [[Continuum limit|scaling limit]] of cluster interfaces in critical FK Ising percolation.
*CLE<sub>6</sub> is a scaling limit of [[percolation theory|critical percolation]] on the triangular lattice.

==Constructions==

For 8/3 < κ < 8, CLE<sub>κ</sub> may be constructed using a branching variation of an SLE<sub>κ</sub> process.<ref>{{harvnb|Sheffield|2009}}</ref>  When 8/3 < κ ≤ 4, CLE<sub>κ</sub> may be alternatively constructed as the collection of outer boundaries of Brownian loop soup clusters.<ref>{{harvnb|Sheffield|Werner|2010}}</ref>

==Properties==

CLE<sub>κ</sub> is conformally invariant, which means that if <math>\varphi:D\to D'</math> is a [[conformal map]], then the law of a CLE in ''D''' is the same as the law of the image of all the CLE loops in ''D'' under the map <math>\varphi</math>.

Since CLE<sub>κ</sub> may be defined using an SLE<sub>κ</sub> process, CLE loops inherit many path properties from SLE. For example, each CLE<sub>κ</sub> loop is a fractal with almost-sure [[Hausdorff dimension]] 1&nbsp;+&nbsp;''κ''/8. Each loop is almost surely simple (no self intersections) when 8/3 < κ ≤ 4 and almost surely self-touching when 4 < ''κ'' < 8.

The set of all points not surrounded by any loop, which is called the ''gasket'', has Hausdorff dimension 1 + 2/''κ'' + 3''κ''/32 almost surely (random soups, carpets and fractal dimensions by Nacu and Werner.<ref>{{harvnb|Miller|Sun|Wilson|2012}}</ref> Since this dimension is strictly greater than 1+κ/8, there are almost surely points not contained in or surrounded by any loop. However, since the gasket dimension is strictly less than 2, [[almost all]] points (with respect to area measure) are contained in the interior of a loop.

CLE is sometimes defined to include only the outermost loops, so that the collection of loops is non-nested (no loop is contained in another). Such a CLE is called a ''simple'' CLE to distinguish it from a ''full'' or ''nested'' CLE. The law of a full CLE can be recovered from the law of a simple CLE as follows. Sample a collection of simple CLE loops, and inside each loop sample another collection of simple CLE loops. Infinitely many iterations of this procedure gives a full CLE.
